culture_principles.name: Public mission and customer-impact alignment
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow fit should connect work to the company outcomes and users described in cited public sources.

culture_principles.name: Evidence-backed execution
culture_principles.description: Strong answers should show practical judgment, clear tradeoffs, ownership, and outcomes rather than generic enthusiasm.

culture_principles.name: Trust as the foundation
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow says trust underpins how it works with customers, people, partners, and communities, and turns that into five expectations covering transparency, responsibility, understanding, supervision, and teamwork.

culture_principles.name: AI that works for people
culture_principles.description: The company says its AI products should enhance human abilities and keep users in control, with human-centered, inclusive, transparent, and accountable principles guiding development.

culture_principles.name: Responsibility for the impact of the work
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow's ethics material says teams stand behind what they build, compete fairly, reject corruption, and accept responsibility for the impact of their work.

culture_principles.name: Measurable impact, not just commitments
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow publishes quantified global-impact measures such as renewable electricity, carbon-neutral cloud, social investment, and volunteer participation alongside its commitments.

culture_principles.name: Talent and AI enablement are connected
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow's executive structure combines people leadership with AI enablement, learning, and workforce innovation, suggesting capability building is treated as part of AI adoption.

hiring_signals.signal: Connects decisions to the users, customers, products, or markets named in public company sources.
Uses concrete examples to show ownership, learning, and measurable improvement.
Substantiates claims with accurate, verifiable detail rather than broad assertions.
Explains how AI or automation keeps a human in control and where oversight must remain.
Raises concerns and challenges decisions constructively instead of staying silent.
Connects technical or product choices to measurable customer and business outcomes, including how impact will be tracked.
Shows inclusive collaboration, such as using varied perspectives or data sets to reduce bias in a decision.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Generic admiration for the company without a concrete role, customer, product, or business mechanism.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public lens usage should stay grounded in cited source signals and role-relevant evidence.

anti_signals.anti_signal: AI enthusiasm with no account of governance, oversight, or who remains accountable.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow publicly grounds AI development in human control and accountability, so governance-free AI narratives miss a stated emphasis; this is a preparation signal, not an official disqualifier.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Citing metrics or outcomes that cannot be traced to a source, method, or verification step.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The company's ethics code explicitly ties transparency to honest statements and accurate reporting.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Avoiding disagreement or escalation when a concern is material.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow's ethics framework says speaking up is encouraged and concerns are acted on, with leaders expected to listen.

interview_patterns.pattern: Use cited public source signals to test role-relevant judgment, ownership, communication, and impact.

honest_limits: This is a lightweight public-source lens and does not represent an official ServiceNow hiring standard.
It contains source metadata and non-verbatim public-safe signals only.
Role, team, seniority, location, and hiring manager can materially change interview emphasis.
This lens requires deeper multi-source validation before being promoted to FULLY_DISTILLED.
